improvement_detail: large gains when a small generating set exists (up to 614x fewer probes; on associative inputs at n = 512 Light incl. generating set is 235-340x faster and the anchored test 565x faster than the exhaustive check, indicative timings); essentially none on left-zero bands (1.7x); randomised tests trade certainty for O(n^2) cost
limitations: Families chosen to include worst cases for each method; no comparison with optimised C implementations.
novelty_basis: The algorithms are classical (Light; Rajagopalan-Schulman); the benchmark is ours. Timings were measured on a shared, loaded machine and are indicative only; probe counts are exact.
statement: On cyclic groups, anchored tables, random magmas and their one-entry corruptions (n = 32..512), Light's test with a greedy generating set uses 23-614 times fewer table probes than the exhaustive n^3 check (generating-set cost included) and the anchored test 2n^2 probes; on left-zero bands the gain is only 1.7x. The randomised test (40 rounds) made no error; random-triple sampling with n^2/16 samples missed 27 of 30 near-associative inputs.
title: Benchmark - generator and anchor tests versus the exhaustive check
